title: Proper pushforward of a bounded coherent finite-Tor complex is perfect
statement: Let S be a Noetherian scheme [def-pc-scheme], let f:X\to S be a morphism locally of finite type, and let E be an object of D(\mathcal O_X) [def-pc-derived-category]. Assume E is bounded with coherent cohomology sheaves, every cohomology sheaf of E has support proper over S [def-weil-pbc-closed-subset-proper-over-base], and E has finite Tor dimension as an object of D(f^{-1}\mathcal O_S). Then Rf_*E [def-pc-derived-direct-image] is a perfect object of D(\mathcal O_S) [def-pc-perfect-complex].

proof.text: The hypotheses on S, f, and E, including bounded coherent cohomology and proper support of every cohomology sheaf, are exactly those of [lem-pc-direct-image-bounded-coherent]. Therefore Rf_*E has bounded coherent cohomology on S.

proof.text: Since S is Noetherian, [lem-pc-noetherian-bounded-coherent-pseudo-coherent] turns the bounded coherent cohomology from Step 1 into pseudo-coherence of Rf_*E.

proof.text: The hypothesis that E has finite Tor dimension over f^{-1}\mathcal O_S concerns E on X, not Rf_*E on S; the passage between them is [lem-pc-proper-direct-image-finite-tor], whose hypotheses (S Noetherian, f locally of finite type, E bounded with coherent cohomology, every cohomology sheaf with support proper over S, E of finite Tor dimension in D(f^{-1}\mathcal O_S)) are exactly those of the statement. Hence Rf_*E has finite Tor dimension as an object of D(\mathcal O_S). In Lean the cited finite-Tor lemma uses a common morphism universe for both derived localizations. Choose a complex K representing E by essential surjectivity of Q. The homology factorization identifies its cohomology in the original and standard localizations; finite generation and coherence are transported by finite local generators and the kernel isomorphism for postcomposition with an isomorphism, and proper support by the stalk isomorphisms. The relative finite-Tor witness is transported by Mathlib Localization.uniq and Localization.compUniqFunctor. Replace bounds a,b by min(a,b),b to obtain ordered bounds. Apply the cited theorem in the standard source and target localizations. By [def-pc-ringed-spaces-derived-direct-image], the K-injective factorization identifies both versions of the direct image with Q(f_*I(K)), using exactly the same complex f_*I(K). Transport each K-flat representative and its localization isomorphism back along Localization.uniq; the tensor complexes and their homology remain unchanged. This gives finite Tor dimension in the original target localization, without changing any hypothesis.
